minutes.headline: Commission approved a 990 Mass Ave permit after the chimney and windows were already removed, flagging the process gap
minutes.summary: The Architectural Preservation District Commission approved two determinations of applicability — 990 Mass Ave and 3 Oak Ave — with the 990 Mass Ave approval noting that demolition work had already occurred before review, and heard from the applicant, Tanner Cole, about asbestos-driven window removal and newly discovered roof-framing problems. The commission also continued pressing the owner of the 50 Main Street church about repairing its deteriorating steeple and set its next meeting for 9 July.

what_happened.line: Commission approved a permit for 990 Mass Ave after the chimney and windows had already been removed, noting the work proceeded before review.
It separately approved a barn shingle replacement at 3 Oak Ave.
The 990 Mass Ave applicant said window removal followed an asbestos finding and questioned whether all approvals, including a zoning appeal window, were complete first.
The chair will ask the planning board and the town's land use director how the district bylaw's "use" language applies to a single-family-to-multi-family conversion.
The commission kept open its push for the 50 Main Street church owner to repair a deteriorating steeple, watching for July.

why_it_matters: A property owner who removes historic features before a preservation review still received approval afterward, which bears on what the district's review actually stops.
The open question of whether the bylaw's "use" language covers a conversion to multi-family could shape future permit decisions in the district.
The church steeple's disrepair is unresolved and will be checked again next meeting for whether repair work has started.
